csp_grade.issue_base_uri_missing: base-uri missing: an injected base tag can hijack relative links
csp_grade.issue_default_src_missing: default-src missing: other resource types are not restricted
csp_grade.issue_form_action_open: form-action missing or open: an injected form can send its data elsewhere
csp_grade.issue_frame_ancestors_missing: frame-ancestors missing (and no X-Frame-Options): any site can frame the page
csp_grade.issue_no_script_policy: No rule restricts scripts (neither script-src nor default-src)
csp_grade.issue_object_src_missing: object-src missing (and no default-src): plugins are not blocked
csp_grade.issue_script_bypass_host: {directive} trusts {host}, which hosts known bypass vectors
csp_grade.issue_script_scheme: {directive} allows a whole scheme (http: or https:)
csp_grade.score_absent: No CSP (already counted in the security headers)
csp_grade.score_report_only: CSP in report-only mode: no protection enforced
finding.csp_grade.report_only: The CSP is report-only (Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only): it blocks nothing.
module.csp_grade.checks: Grades from A to F the Content-Security-Policy actually enforced (header and meta tag): script execution, nonces and hashes, base-uri, object-src, frame-ancestors, form-action.
module.csp_grade.fix:
Start in observation mode: send the new policy in the `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` header (see the snippet) and read in the browser console (F12 key) what it would block, without breaking anything. Adjust until the important pages no longer produce a warning.
When the policy is clean, enforce it by renaming the header to `Content-Security-Policy`: report-only mode blocks nothing. Send the CSP as an HTTP header rather than a `meta` tag, which ignores `frame-ancestors`.
In `script-src` (or `default-src` if there is none), remove the flagged overly broad sources: `*`, `http:`, `https:`, `data:`, `blob:`, `filesystem:`, `'unsafe-eval'` and `'unsafe-hashes'`, as well as public hosts that serve known bypasses (`cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`, `*.googleapis.com`, `*.amazonaws.com`...). Keep only your own origins.
Replace `'unsafe-inline'`: move inline scripts into `.js` files, or allow them with a random nonce generated for every response (`script-src 'nonce-VALUE' 'strict-dynamic'`, with the `nonce` attribute on `script` tags), or with a hash (`'sha256-...'`) for a fixed inline script. Do the same for `style-src`.
Complete the directives that do not fall back to `default-src`: `base-uri 'none'` (or `'self'`), `form-action 'self'` and `frame-ancestors 'self'` (or `'none'` if the page must never be framed), then add `object-src 'none'` and a fallback `default-src 'self'`.
If a third-party service requires an exception (payment, chat, analytics), add only its exact domain to the relevant directive, and write down why: every exception weakens the protection.
Check: `curl -sI https://example.com | grep -i content-security-policy` must show the policy; check in the browser console that no legitimate resource is blocked, then run the scan again to get the new grade.
module.csp_grade.fix_snippet:
# nginx
add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'" always;

# nginx Report-Only
add_header Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'" always;

# Apache
Header always set Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'"

# IIS
<system.webServer>
  <httpProtocol>
    <customHeaders>
      <add name="Content-Security-Policy" value="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'" />
    </customHeaders>
  </httpProtocol>
</system.webServer>

# Caddy
example.com {
    header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'"
}
module.csp_grade.title: CSP grade
module.csp_grade.why: A well-built CSP stops an injected script from running (XSS). A CSP that allows “*” or 'unsafe-inline' gives a false sense of security.
